recognize_zh: 大量中至大型芽細胞，細胞質深嗜鹼性且周邊有明顯的出芽狀突起（cytoplasmic blebs），核染色質細緻、可見核仁，背景有血小板團塊；在 Down 症兒童身上，這種巨核芽細胞（megakaryoblast）型態即指向 ML-DS。
features: Medium to large blasts with moderate N:C ratio and round to slightly irregular nuclei
Fine, dispersed chromatin with one or more visible nucleoli
Deeply basophilic, agranular cytoplasm with prominent cytoplasmic blebs and pseudopod-like budding
Occasional smaller dark blast/lymphoid-appearing cells admixed
Clumps of granular platelet/megakaryocytic material in the background
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear shows numerous medium to large blasts with fine chromatin, visible nucleoli and deeply basophilic, agranular cytoplasm bearing conspicuous cytoplasmic blebs. Aggregates of platelet-like granular material are present in the background. Auer rods and cytoplasmic granulation are not seen. The morphology is that of megakaryoblasts; in a child with Down syndrome, findings are consistent with myeloid leukemia associated with Down syndrome (acute megakaryoblastic type), to be confirmed by flow cytometry (CD41/CD61) and GATA1 mutation analysis.

ddx.vs: TAM shows morphologically identical megakaryoblasts but occurs in neonates (usually <3 months) and often regresses spontaneously; age and clinical course, not morphology, separate them.
Morphology overlaps; separation relies on absence of trisomy 21/GATA1 mutation and presence of t(1;22).
Lymphoblasts have scant, less basophilic cytoplasm without blebs and are CD19/CD79a/TdT positive rather than CD41/CD61 positive.

ddx.dx: Metastatic small round blue cell tumor (e.g., neuroblastoma)
ddx.vs: Tumor cells form cohesive clusters/rosettes with molding and are negative for CD41/CD61 and CD45.
